analysis.investment_thesis: INOX India is a genuinely good niche business — 48 years of cryogenic engineering expertise, 38% ROCE, near-zero debt — but at 53x trailing P/E with only 12% revenue CAGR and free cash flow turning negative in FY25, the price demands perfection with no margin of safety. I admire the business; I do not admire the price tag.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital returns: ROCE 38%, ROE 29%, operating margins ~20% — hallmarks of a real competitive moat in specialized cryogenic engineering
Near-pristine balance sheet: D/E compressed from 0.52 (FY20) to 0.10 (FY25), finance costs collapsed from INR 27 Cr to INR 9 Cr, promoters hold 75%
Secular demand tailwinds across LNG, green hydrogen, and aerospace/ISRO supply chain — diversified across 20+ critical end-sectors
key_risks: Valuation leaves zero margin of safety: 53x P/E, 41x EV/EBITDA, and 13.8x P/B for a business growing revenue at 12% CAGR is a recipe for disappointment if growth falters
FCF deteriorating sharply: from INR 175 Cr (FY20) to -INR 3 Cr (FY25) as capex surged to INR 125 Cr — the business is in an investment cycle and cash generation is stretched
Net profit 6-year CAGR is only 2.7% (INR 193→226 Cr) — much of historical earnings were boosted by lumpy 'other income' (INR 28–48 Cr), masking the true operating earnings power
red_flags: Free cash flow went negative (-INR 3 Cr) in FY25 with capex accelerating to INR 125 Cr — at a 53x P/E multiple, the market is pricing in flawless execution of this investment cycle
Borrowings jumped from INR 16 Cr (FY24) to INR 99 Cr (FY25) — early but worth monitoring given the prior debt reduction narrative that helped re-rate the stock
analysis.detailed_analysis:
INOX India is the kind of niche industrial business I find intellectually interesting. It has built a genuine technical moat in cryogenic equipment over nearly five decades — the sort of specialized know-how that competitors cannot replicate quickly. The return metrics confirm this: 38% ROCE and 29% ROE are exceptional for an industrial manufacturer, and the company has steadily scrubbed its balance sheet clean, bringing D/E from 0.52 to 0.10. Promoter ownership at 75% is a strong alignment signal. The exposure to LNG infrastructure, green hydrogen, and Indian space programs (ISRO) gives it credible secular growth drivers that most industrial peers lack.

The problem, as it almost always is with good businesses I encounter on the market, is the price. At 53x trailing earnings and 41x EV/EBITDA for a company growing revenues at 12% per annum, the market has already priced in a very rosy future. Worse, free cash flow turned negative in FY25 (-INR 3 Cr) as the company pushed capex to INR 125 Cr — meaning the business is now consuming rather than generating cash during this expansion phase. If the capex cycle delivers, the stock may prove justified in hindsight; but I never pay for hopes and promises when the current price already reflects them. At roughly 25–28x P/E, this would become an interesting conversation. At 53x, I'll watch from the sidelines.
